title: cloudflare-auth ships settings.py and config.py with divergent CloudflareSettings; dead module is test-only
evidence: Production imports cloudflare_auth.config; tests import cloudflare_auth.settings; the two CloudflareSettings classes diverge on env aliases (CF_* vs CLOUDFLARE_*), require_cloudflare_headers default (True vs False), and certs_url. Tests validate a module the package does not ship.
recommendation: Delete settings.py, repoint its tests to config.py, and reconcile the env-var contract before publishing.

title: CI tests only 2 of 4 packages; cloudflare-api and gemini-image published with no CI
evidence: ci.yml defines test jobs only for cloudflare-auth (line 63) and gcs-utilities (line 111); detect-changes (51-60) lists only those two. cloudflare-api and gemini-image are published to Artifact Registry with zero test, lint, or type-check in CI.
recommendation: Add test-cloudflare-api and test-gemini-image jobs and path filters mirroring the existing two; wire both into ci-gate.

title: Coverage gate disabled in CI (--cov-fail-under=0) while house standard is 80%
evidence: Both CI test jobs pass --cov-fail-under=0 plus --no-cov-on-fail; release.yml uses 80%. A regression dropping coverage to near zero passes CI and only fails at release.
recommendation: Set --cov-fail-under=80 in both CI jobs, or enforce a combined threshold in ci-gate.

title: Coverage artifact name mismatch silently breaks Codecov/Qlty uploads
evidence: CI uploads coverage-cloudflare-auth and coverage-gcs-utilities; the workflow_run consumers expect a single artifact named coverage-reports. No step produces coverage-reports, so downstream uploads process nothing.
recommendation: Rename CI artifacts to coverage-reports (merged XML) or change the three consumers to a coverage-* pattern.

title: Bandit runs with || true, so security findings never fail CI
evidence: ci.yml:181 Bandit step ends in || true; the Security Scan job always passes. Contradicts CLAUDE.md 'fail on HIGH/CRITICAL by default'.
recommendation: Remove || true from the Bandit step; assert_used config already skips test asserts so a failure is signal.

title: Vulnerable production crypto/auth deps at locked versions (pyjwt, cryptography, starlette)
evidence: uvx pip-audit 2.10.0 against exported lock: pyjwt 2.10.1 (PYSEC-2026-120, fix 2.12.0), cryptography 46.0.3 (CVE-2026-26007/PYSEC-2026-35/36, fix 46.0.7), starlette 0.50.0 (PYSEC-2026-161, fix 1.0.1). Open version floors mean a re-resolve pulls fixes.
recommendation: Re-resolve the lock and confirm fixed versions; verify FastAPI compatibility before the starlette major bump. Re-run pip-audit to confirm advisories are current.

title: Lockfile stale ~5.5 months; reproducible but out of date, root cause of persisting CVEs
evidence: uv.lock last modified by commit 2d84e06 on 2025-12-15; HEAD is 2026-05-07. Open >= floors mean DEP-01/DEP-02 fixes exist upstream but were never re-resolved into the lock.
recommendation: Run uv lock, commit, re-audit; add a scheduled uv lock --upgrade plus pip-audit job so drift is caught.

title: Handoff doc says cloudflare-api belongs in another repo while README ships it as first-class
evidence: cloudflare-api-handoff.md:14 states the package 'was developed in the wrong repository ... ready for migration to homelab-infra'; README.md:46 lists it as maintained and it is a live workspace member.
recommendation: Decide ownership: if it stays, delete the handoff doc and add a normal package README/ADR.

title: IP allowlist uses string prefix matching, not CIDR
evidence: client_ip.startswith(allowed_ip.rstrip('/') + '.') is a string test: a 10.0.0.0/8 entry becomes prefix 10.0.0.0. and matches nothing, while a short 10.0 over-matches. No IPv6 handling. Sibling cloudflare-api already has correct ipaddress-based logic.
recommendation: Use ipaddress.ip_address(client_ip) in ipaddress.ip_network(allowed_ip, strict=False); reject unparseable entries at config load; add subnet/IPv6 tests.

title: Five independent exception hierarchies reimplement one message+context+serialize pattern
evidence: ProjectBaseError(to_dict, error_code, details), CloudflareAPIError(code, errors, response), and GCSError(bare pass) solve the same concern with incompatible constructors; cross-package error handling needs two attribute sets.
recommendation: Reparent per-package errors onto the existing ProjectBaseError, or at minimum align the message/details/error_code/to_dict contract.

title: Two full middleware implementations; original superseded but still exported
evidence: middleware_enhanced.py does not subclass middleware.py; both define their own BaseHTTPMiddleware subclass, setup function, and get_current_user with copy-and-evolve bodies. __init__ exports both classes but only the enhanced setup.
recommendation: Remove middleware.py or make enhanced extend it so shared request/JWT logic lives once; export one get_current_user.

title: Placeholder assert-True tests; package tests cannot run in-env; 99% coverage figure covers ~1% of code
evidence: Root suite reports 99.32% but only covers src/python_libs (115 statements); the four packages (>9000 LOC) are excluded. cloudflare-auth tests fail collection (no fastapi). Three assert True placeholders; pytest-cov not installed so documented pytest --cov is broken.
recommendation: Add pytest-cov and package runtime deps to the dev group, scope the 80% gate across all packages, and replace or delete the placeholder tests.

title: CLAUDE.md Project Structure omits all 4 packages where shipped code lives
evidence: CLAUDE.md tree is rooted at src/python_libs/ and never mentions packages/{cloudflare-auth,cloudflare-api,gcs-utilities,gemini-image}; coverage example uses --cov=src. Agents following it look in the wrong place.
recommendation: Replace the structure block with the real monorepo layout and fix coverage examples to span packages.

title: CONTRIBUTING.md describes a single-package layout that does not exist
evidence: CONTRIBUTING tree shows src/python_libs/ with a core.py file (reality is core/ directory); the import example from python_libs.core import YourModule is a non-existent symbol. No packages/ mention.
recommendation: Rewrite the structure section for the monorepo and replace fake import examples with a real one.

title: API reference documents only the optional shared package, none of the 4 published packages
evidence: api-reference.md has two autodoc blocks (python_libs.core.config, python_libs.utils.logging); the 4 shipped packages have none. mkdocs paths: [src] cannot resolve packages/*/src symbols.
recommendation: Add packages/*/src to mkdocstrings paths and add per-package API pages to nav.

title: CSRF validation never verifies the session-bound HMAC token
evidence: generate_token builds an HMAC bound to session_id, but validate_token only does secrets.compare_digest(cookie_token, header_token); it never re-derives the HMAC or checks session binding. Scheme degrades to plain double-submit. token_bytes(32) at csrf.py:82 is dead.
recommendation: Recompute and verify the HMAC from session id and secret_key in validate_token (or validate against a server-side store); remove the dead token_bytes call; add rejection tests.

title: Umbrella python_libs core is dead weight; no package depends on it
evidence: Repo-wide grep for python_libs inside packages/ returns nothing; no package lists the umbrella as a dependency, and it is not a workspace member. core/exceptions.py defines the base every package reimplements yet is imported by nobody outside the umbrella.
recommendation: Either make the four packages depend on python_libs and reuse its base error/config/logging, or delete src/python_libs/core and utils if packages are standalone.

title: BasedPyright not installed; cloudflare-auth carries 513 strict warnings, 13 errors, 81 Any uses
evidence: uv run basedpyright fails (not installed). Run via --with: src 0 errors/21 warnings; cloudflare-auth 13 errors/513 warnings (errors are unresolved optional imports). Any appears 81 times across 18 source files; 6 type:ignore plus 1 pyright:ignore.
recommendation: Add basedpyright to the dev group, install package optional deps for analysis, then drive reportAny warnings down starting with client.py and fetchers.py.

title: middleware.py and middleware_enhanced.py are near-duplicate (11 shared methods, ~27% of package)
evidence: The two files share 11 identically named methods (dispatch, _authenticate_request, _check_rate_limit, get_current_user, etc.); together 1,309 LOC, roughly 27% of the package's 4,887 LOC.
recommendation: Collapse to one middleware gated by config flags, or extract the shared methods into a base class.

title: CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING omit the packages/ monorepo (overlaps DOC-03)
evidence: CLAUDE.md Project Structure shows only src/python_libs/; CONTRIBUTING never mentions monorepo/packages/workspace; ADR-001 documents the workspace monorepo, so the onboarding doc contradicts the intended structure.
recommendation: Rewrite the CLAUDE.md structure section to show packages/* as the primary code location and add a CONTRIBUTING section on per-package layout.

title: Pre-commit lacks the Ruff and BasedPyright hooks CI enforces
evidence: Lines 134-135 are comments naming Ruff and BasedPyright but no such hook exists; CI enforces both. Ruff/type checks route through the qlty hook, which is in the pre-commit.ci skip list, so hosted runs skip them too.
recommendation: Add astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit (check + format) and a BasedPyright hook, or confirm qlty runs Ruff in the commit path.

title: 12 org reusable workflows pinned to mutable @main (overlaps SEC-04)
evidence: 41/41 third-party actions are SHA-pinned, but 12 callers of ByronWilliamsCPA/.github reusable workflows use @main; two already pin to a SHA. A reusable workflow can swap the leaf actions it runs, defeating leaf pinning.
recommendation: Pin all 12 to a SHA or release tag as the two already done; let Renovate bump them.

title: Path filters and scan targets watch src/ while code lives in packages/
evidence: python-compatibility, fips-compatibility, and mutation-testing path-trigger on src/**/*.py only; Sonar source-directory is src; basedpyright/Bandit/Vulture targets are src. None run on package-only changes, so the four packages are unscanned on package PRs.
recommendation: Add packages/** to path filters and point source-directory and scan targets at packages.

title: Python version drift across docs (3.12 vs 3.10-3.14)
evidence: pyproject and PYTHON_COMPATIBILITY say 3.10-3.14; CLAUDE.md:36 says 3.12, README badge says 3.12 (body text correctly says 3.10+), index.md says 3.12+.
recommendation: State '3.10-3.14 (3.12 recommended)' consistently in CLAUDE.md, the README badge, and index.md.

title: Planning README still marks docs 'Awaiting Generation' though all are written
evidence: The status table marks project-vision, tech-spec, roadmap, adr as 'Awaiting Generation' but all four exist with real content (project-vision 112 lines, tech-spec 292, roadmap 269, 3 accepted ADRs).
recommendation: Update the status column to Complete/Active with dates so the work is not re-run and overwritten.

title: README references a missing .claude/claude.md and a .claude/standard/ subtree that do not exist
evidence: README references .claude/claude.md (actual is .claude/README.md) and documents a .claude/standard/ git subtree with a subtree pull command; the directory does not exist. The project uses cruft + .standards/ instead.
recommendation: Remove the subtree section or replace it with the actual cruft/.standards workflow; fix the .claude path.

title: Install/usage docs reference a nonexistent python-libs PyPI package and placeholder imports
evidence: index.md:17 says pip install python-libs (never published; repo publishes 4 byronwilliamscpa-* packages to Artifact Registry). README Basic Usage uses from python_libs import YourModule, a placeholder symbol.
recommendation: Replace with the per-package install and a real import example.

title: SECURITY.md required by project standards is absent from repo root
evidence: CLAUDE.md 'Required Project Files' lists SECURITY.md as mandatory; no SECURITY.md exists at root. README and CONTRIBUTING redirect to the org-level policy, which conflicts with the repo's own requirement and Scorecard's expectation of a discoverable policy.
recommendation: Add a local SECURITY.md (a stub linking to the org policy satisfies Scorecard) or amend the Required Project Files list to note org delegation.

title: Naive datetime defaults in field factories (latent TypeError in IP-cache path)
evidence: Both fields default to datetime.now (naive) while surrounding code is tz-aware UTC. manager.py:158 subtracts a naive default from an aware now, raising TypeError if the default is ever used; models.py:149 records local wall-clock for an auth timestamp.
recommendation: Use default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc) for both; the manager case is a correctness bug.

title: Reusable org workflows pinned to mutable @main while leaf actions are SHA-pinned
evidence: Third-party actions are SHA-pinned, but first-party reusable workflows mostly use @main; two are already SHA-pinned, proving inconsistency. pr-validation.yml and release.yml pass secrets: inherit, so a force-push to .github main reaches this repo's secrets.
recommendation: Pin every reusable-workflow uses: to a commit SHA with a version comment; let Renovate keep them current.

title: Two session managers with no shared interface; redis variant import-guarded not abstracted
evidence: SimpleSessionManager and RedisSessionManager share no base or Protocol; middleware_enhanced.py and security_helpers.py hardwire SimpleSessionManager. A backing-store choice modeled as two disconnected types.
recommendation: Define a SessionManager Protocol both implement and have the middleware depend on it so Redis is a drop-in.

title: Inconsistent error and config patterns across packages (gemini-image raises raw stdlib errors)
evidence: gemini-image has no exceptions module and raises stdlib ValueError/FileNotFoundError/ImportError; cloudflare-api splits config between env BaseSettings and YAML BaseModel with no stated rule on which to use.
recommendation: Add gemini_image/exceptions.py with a package base; document or consolidate the env-vs-YAML config split.

title: Static-analysis Python-version drift across four tool/matrix sets
evidence: Code claims 3.10-3.14; Ruff/BasedPyright/Sonar validate only 3.12; CI tests 3.10-3.13; nox tests 3.10-3.14. Ruff target-version py312 means 3.10/3.11-incompatible syntax is not flagged.
recommendation: Pick one floor; if 3.10 is real set Ruff target-version to py310 so down-level checks fire, and align nox/CI/compat matrices.

title: Redundant coverage destinations and duplicate Qlty caller
evidence: Coverage ships to Codecov (inline plus a dedicated caller), Qlty (qlty.yml and coverage.yml both call the same reusable workflow), and SonarCloud. Duplicated minutes and duplicate PR comments.
recommendation: Pick one coverage host; remove coverage.yml or qlty.yml and drop one of the two Codecov paths.

title: Each package reimplements its own exception hierarchy; shared core hierarchy unused
evidence: grep for 'from python_libs' across packages/ returns nothing; to_dict serialization exists only in core and is not reused. Violates the CLAUDE.md 'Reuse First' principle.
recommendation: Have package exceptions subclass the core hierarchy, or document that packages stay standalone and drop the unused core module from the shared-value claim.

title: Repeated settings singleton/global boilerplate across packages; duplicate CloudflareSettings name
evidence: The global _settings_instance + reset_settings pattern is hand-copied across cloudflare_api/settings.py, cloudflare_auth/settings.py, csrf.py, rate_limiter.py, security_helpers.py (two PLW0603 ruff findings). cloudflare-auth defines CloudflareSettings twice.
recommendation: Provide a single cached_settings/reset helper in core and reuse it; pick one CloudflareSettings (see ARCH-03).

title: Complexity hotspots over the C901 limit; four files exceed 700 LOC
evidence: ruff C901 (limit 10) flags _auto_extract_ips at 11; lowering to 6 surfaces 16 functions in the 7-11 band. Worst files by length: whitelist.py 787, gcs client.py 759, middleware_enhanced.py 740, cloudflare-api client.py 676.
recommendation: Split _auto_extract_ips into typed handlers, decompose validate_token/get_user_tier, and treat the four 700+ LOC files as refactor candidates.

title: Vulnerable transitive and dev-tool dependencies (60 advisory rows across 30 packages)
evidence: uvx pip-audit: production-reachable transitives urllib3 2.5.0 (fix 2.7.0), idna 3.11 (fix 3.15), requests 2.32.5 (fix 2.33.0), protobuf 6.33.1 (fix 6.33.5), pyasn1 0.6.1 (fix 0.6.3); plus a jupyter/nltk/safety dev cluster. SBOM gate fails only on CRITICAL/HIGH so Mediums pass.
recommendation: Re-resolve to pull fixed transitive versions; lower the SBOM fail threshold to include MEDIUM or document why not.

title: Inconsistent Python version policy; 3.10 EOL Oct 2026; 3.14 declared but untested
evidence: requires-python >=3.10,<3.15 (ceiling 3.14), CI matrix stops at 3.13, classifiers stop at 3.13, Ruff/BasedPyright pinned to 3.12, CLAUDE.md says 3.12. Python 3.10 reaches EOL in October 2026 (~5 months out).
recommendation: Pick one policy: add 3.14 to CI and classifiers or lower the ceiling; plan to drop the 3.10 floor by its EOL; align CLAUDE.md.

title: Missing ADRs for dual middleware and redis sessions; two ADR directories
evidence: ADR-001..003 cover monorepo/framework/distribution but nothing explains dual middleware or the redis session backend. docs/ADRs/ (root) holds only template files while real ADRs live in docs/planning/adr/; README points at the empty one.
recommendation: Add ADRs for the dual-middleware and redis-session choices; consolidate or cross-link the two ADR directories and point README at the populated one.

title: get_client_ip trusts CF-Connecting-IP regardless of upstream
evidence: CF-Connecting-IP header is read unconditionally; if the service is reachable directly any client can forge it. The value feeds the rate limiter and IP allowlist, so a spoofed header defeats throttling and may satisfy the tunnel allowlist.
recommendation: Honor CF-Connecting-IP only when request.client.host is in a configured trusted-proxy range; make the trust boundary explicit in settings.

title: Workspace declares cross-package sources that nothing uses
evidence: [tool.uv.sources] marks all four distributions workspace=true 'to allow packages to depend on each other', but no package lists another or the umbrella in dependencies. The declared coupling channel is untested scaffolding.
recommendation: Remove the unused source entries until a real cross-package dependency exists, or add the dependency that ARCH-01/ARCH-02 imply.

title: setup-uv version skew and mislabeled SHA version comments
evidence: One setup-uv SHA carries two different version comments (# v4 in 7 uses, # v4.2.0 in codeql.yml:52); one workflow runs v6.8.0. checkout SHA 34e1148 is labeled both # v4 and # v4.3.1.
recommendation: Normalize on one setup-uv major across all workflows and fix the mislabeled comments; Renovate keeps them aligned.

title: Formatter width disagreements between Prettier, markdownlint, and yamllint
evidence: Python 88 is consistent. Markdown: CLAUDE.md/Prettier say 120 but markdownlint disables MD013. YAML: Prettier printWidth 120 vs yamllint max 150 (warning). No hard conflict, three sources disagree.
recommendation: Set .yamllint line-length max to 120 to match Prettier and decide whether markdownlint should enforce MD013 at 120.

title: 34 standing ruff findings including S104, LOG015, SLF001, str-Enum
evidence: ruff check . reports 34 errors, 6 auto-fixable: 9 TRY300, 5 PERF401, 4 UP042 (str,Enum -> StrEnum), 3 FURB110, 3 PLC0207, 2 PLW0603, 2 SIM117, plus single C901/LOG015/RUF022/S104/SIM102/SLF001. S104 binds all interfaces; LOG015 root-logger call contradicts structured-logging convention.
recommendation: Run ruff check . --fix for the 6 safe fixes, migrate the four (str, Enum) classes to StrEnum, confirm S104 is intentional.

title: Few but stale TODO markers (2025-12-14); one disabled CI secrets path
evidence: ~21 TODO-family hits, mostly template scaffolding; only two actionable: a placeholder test TODO and a 'Re-enable Infisical once Cloudflare Access is configured' TODO in publish CI. Both date to 2025-12-14, ~5.5 months old.
recommendation: Resolve the test placeholder (see CQ-06) and convert the Infisical CI TODO into a tracked issue.

title: Abandoned dev-transitive package py 1.11.0 (last release 2021)
evidence: py 1.11.0 resolved with upload-time 2021-11-04 (~4.5 years, unmaintained); pip-audit flags the disputed PYSEC-2022-42969. Dev-only transitive, already excepted in osv-scanner.toml. The only dependency past the 18-month-no-release line.
recommendation: Keep the documented exception, or pin the consuming dev tool to a version that has dropped py. No production exposure.

title: SBOM workflow unpinned @main, MEDIUM advisories not gated, pip-audit not run in CI
evidence: sbom.yml delegates to an org reusable workflow pinned @main with security-events: write; severity-threshold CRITICAL,HIGH lets ~25 Medium advisories pass; pip-audit is a declared dev dep but no workflow runs it.
recommendation: Pin the reusable workflow to a SHA, lower the fail threshold to include MEDIUM, and add a scheduled lock-refresh plus pip-audit gate.

title: No migration residue (confirming finding)
evidence: find and git ls-files for requirements*.txt, setup.py, setup.cfg, poetry.lock, Pipfile all return nothing. Cleanly on PEP 621 + uv. scripts/generate_requirements.sh produces requirements on demand but commits none.
recommendation: No action; note that requirements files produced with --no-hashes would bypass the lock's hash pinning.

title: CHANGELOG [0.1.0] - TBD placeholder; uneven per-package changelogs
evidence: CHANGELOG.md:24 reads ## [0.1.0] - TBD while README states current version 0.1.0 and all four packages declare 0.1.0. cloudflare-api and gemini-image have no package CHANGELOG.
recommendation: Set the 0.1.0 date or mark it unreleased clearly; add CHANGELOG stubs to the two packages missing them.

title: timezone.utc instead of datetime.UTC at 31 sites (mixed with one modern use)
evidence: 31 uses of timezone.utc across 9 files; only gemini-image/generator.py uses the 3.11 datetime.UTC shorthand. datetime.UTC requires 3.11 and the floor is 3.10, so a straight swap would break 3.10.
recommendation: Keep timezone.utc everywhere for consistency given the 3.10 floor, or raise the floor to 3.11 and standardize on UTC; do not leave it mixed.

title: Single os.path.exists use where pathlib is the house standard
evidence: One occurrence repo-wide: os.path.exists(self._credentials_path). CLAUDE.md states pathlib is the house standard.
recommendation: Replace with Path(self._credentials_path).exists(); verify whether import os is still needed afterward.

title: No detect-secrets baseline; TruffleHog pre-commit hook no-ops if the binary is absent
evidence: No .secrets.baseline (project uses TruffleHog, not detect-secrets). The local hook prints 'TruffleHog not installed - skipping' and passes when the binary is missing, so pre-commit secret scanning is best-effort. CI security workflows mitigate server-side.
recommendation: Add detect-secrets with a committed baseline, or make the TruffleHog hook fail (not skip) when the binary is missing in CI context.

title: Seven-plus overlapping SAST/dependency scanners for a small library
evidence: Python SAST is covered by CodeQL, SonarCloud, Qlty (wraps Ruff+Bandit), inline Bandit, and Semgrep; dependency vulns by OSV, Safety, dependency-review, and Renovate. High run-cost and review-noise, much stacked Monday mornings.
recommendation: Keep CodeQL plus one of SonarCloud/Qlty, drop the redundant one and the inline Bandit (Qlty already runs Bandit), and document the chosen stack.

title: Large doc set excluded from mkdocs nav (orphaned from the rendered site)
evidence: Not in nav and so unreachable on the built site: OPENSSF_COMPLIANCE, PROJECT_SETUP, PYTHON_COMPATIBILITY, secure.md, the ADRs/ planning/ diagrams/ _data/ trees. strict: false suppresses the warning.
recommendation: Add the onboarding/compliance docs and the planning/ADR section to nav; leave handoff/feedback out or remove them.

title: Actively-maintained parallel basic/enhanced middleware risks double-patching (overlaps ARCH-04/CQ-02)
evidence: Both middleware classes are exported and edited in the same recent commits (52e5c27, 476736c, 2249de5), so 'enhanced' is a live second variant, not a stale fork; the rate-limit fix had to touch both. Sessions/redis_sessions split is legitimate.
recommendation: Confirm both are intentionally supported and factor shared handling into a base, or mark the basic variant deprecated (see ARCH-04).
